notes: Confirmed against the body. It reads status selector 0x20 through accepted get_attribute_context_status_32, initializes two local output slots, then on the helper predicate paths calls three value helpers and stores their low 16 bits at output offsets 0, 2, and 4; returns zero on all paths. The selector read is visible at main_0058.c:20110-20121, stores at 20124-20131, and return at 20134-20137. No indexed caller exists and rg found no direct C callsite.

Confirmed. The body reads status selector 0 and returns 1 for low-byte values 5 or 9; otherwise it reads selector 0x13 and returns 1 for low byte 8; otherwise it calls the unresolved fallback helper and returns its low bit. No indexed caller exists and rg found no direct C callsite.

Confirmed. It gates on status selector 0x14 equal to 4, resolves the global pointer if null, reads the halfword at pointer+0x32, then uses the reciprocal-multiply sequence on (value-6) to call the helper only for values congruent to 6 modulo 7. I exhaustively checked all 65,536 possible uint16 inputs against that condition; no mismatch. It always returns zero. No indexed caller exists and rg found no direct C callsite.

Confirmed. Accepted check_attribute_status_19_equals_4 makes it return 1 immediately. Otherwise it loads/resolves the pointer at global 0x7004651000+0x350, calls f_7001824f30 with x1=0, returns 1 when result bit 31 is clear and 0 when set. No indexed caller exists and rg found no direct C callsite.

Confirmed. The body uses selector 0x39 with an unknown low-bit predicate; on success it calls accepted sum_matching_record_float_values_clamped with selector 0x39, takes VS32(0), and returns that low word tagged with 1 in the high 32 bits; on failure it returns zero. No indexed caller exists and rg found no direct C callsite.
